name: orbit
description: You can't remember everyone. Orbit can. Ask about the people you talk to on Substack and what your writing does, from your own Orbit account.

interface.longDescription:
You can't remember everyone. Orbit can. Orbit keeps track of who you've talked to on Substack, what you discussed, and where things stand, and what your writing does. Ask ChatGPT about your Substack people and your writing, and it answers from your own Orbit data.

With Orbit, you can:

• Know who to talk to: the subscribers who read everything and have never heard from you, five people worth talking to today, and who's gone quiet.

• Get your Substack briefing: Orbit asks once what matters to you, then brings you the people paying attention to you, the conversations slipping away, and the people worth knowing.

• Catch up before you reply: what you and someone talked about before, and the replies still waiting on you.

• See what's working: ask what's working in your Notes lately, whether you're reaching new people or the same ones, and what to do differently next week. Orbit finds the patterns across your Notes and essays and shows your own examples as the evidence.

• Meet the people behind your numbers: who subscribed after each Note or essay, who replied and restacked, and which of them you already talk with.

• Find what you said before: search your Notes, essays and comments for the conversation you know you had.

Every answer links back to Substack.

When you ask, Orbit can also save a private note or tag on a person, clear a reply from your queue, hide someone from your reminders, mark a DM's status, or save your briefing settings and preferences. It never posts, comments, or sends messages on Substack.

Requires an Orbit account. Orbit fills itself in through its Chrome extension while you use Substack as usual; your Substack login stays on your computer. Direct messages are included only if you turn them on.

Orbit is an independent tool and isn't affiliated with Substack.
defaultPrompt: Who should I talk to today?
Help me set up my daily Substack briefing.
What's working in my Notes lately?

positive.description: Notes that brought in subscribers, with the people named
positive.prompt: Which of my notes brought in new subscribers, and who were they?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the notes that gained subscribers, most first, each with the people who subscribed after seeing it, marked new free or new paid, and a link to each note.

positive.description: Notes ranked by new readers reached
positive.prompt: Which of my recent notes reached the most new people?
positive.expected_behavior: Ranks the notes by new readers reached, each with its full text, a link, its posting time, and its stats (reach, profile visits, likes, replies, restacks).

positive.description: Find the owner's own writing by topic
positive.prompt: Find everything I have written about feeling homesick.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the matching essays and notes, including the essay "Homesick in the Place You Live", each with an excerpt and a link.

positive.prompt: Which of my essays brought in paid subscribers?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the essays with their stats; the essays that converted readers name who came in, including new paid subscribers.

positive.description: Context on one person before replying
positive.prompt: What do I know about Maya Okonkwo before I reply to her?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns Maya's profile, Orbit's summary of the relationship, and their real exchanges (including her note about reading on a train), with a link to her Substack profile.

negative.description: Posting to Substack. Orbit has no tool that publishes, so nothing is posted; the assistant says Orbit cannot post and the user posts it on Substack.
negative.prompt: Post this as a Substack note for me: "Rest isn't a reward for finishing."

negative.description: Sending a direct message. Orbit has no tool that sends messages, so nothing is sent; the assistant may read the person's record for context and points to their Substack profile.
negative.prompt: Send Maya Okonkwo a DM thanking her for the essay.

negative.description: A request unrelated to Substack or the user's writing. Orbit is not called.
negative.prompt: What's the weather in Lisbon this weekend?

review.commerce_description: Orbit does not sell anything inside ChatGPT. The plugin works only with an existing Orbit account.

publication.release_notes: The listing says more about what Orbit finds in your Notes and essays, and the website link goes to the ChatGPT setup page.
